title: Hourly to Annual Salary Conversion: ADF Salary Sacrifice and Tax Considerations
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Understand tax, Medicare, super, and how ADF salary sacrifice can affect your take-home pay.
salarySummary: To convert an hourly rate to annual salary, multiply by hours per week (typically 38) and then by 52 weeks, then add superannuation and deduct tax and Medicare levy.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher.

faqs.q: How does ADF salary sacrifice affect my tax?
faqs.a: ADF salary sacrifice allows you to redirect pre-tax salary into benefits like superannuation, reducing your taxable income. Our calculator does not include salary sacrifice; you should consult the ATO or a financial adviser for personalised estimates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

To work out your annual gross salary from an hourly rate, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work a different pattern, adjust accordingly.

For example, if your base hourly rate is $30.00 and you work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Your fortnightly gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280. Knowing your fortnightly amount can help with budgeting, especially if you are paid fortnightly.

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – use the checkbox instead.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, equating to $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. Check your relevant award via [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) to ensure you're being paid correctly.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, while all employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job.

## Including Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is **12%** from 1 July 2026, applied to earnings up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $59,280 annual salary, the super contribution would be $59,280 × 12% = $7,113.60, added to your employer's cost. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross salary is subject to Australian resident tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally **2%** of your taxable income. For 2025–26, single taxpayers with a taxable income below a certain threshold may pay a reduced rate; we use those thresholds as the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate.

Using our example of $59,280 annual gross, the tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($45,000 - $18,200) = $4,020
- 30% on $14,280 ($59,280 - $45,000) = $4,284
- Total tax = $8,304
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,185.60
- Total deductions = $9,489.60
- Estimated take-home pay = $49,790.40

This estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary sacrifice arrangements. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## ADF Salary Sacrifice Considerations

For members of the Australian Defence Force, salary sacrifice is a common way to reduce taxable income by redirecting pre-tax salary into superannuation or other benefits. This is known as **ADF salary sacrifice**. While our hourly-to-annual calculator does not account for salary sacrifice, understanding how it affects your tax can help you plan. By sacrificing a portion of your salary, your taxable income decreases, potentially lowering your marginal tax rate and Medicare levy. However, the super guarantee is still calculated on your ordinary earnings before sacrifice. Always consult the ATO or a financial adviser for personalised advice.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) page is the home of the hourly-to-annual converter. Enter your base hourly rate (before any loading) and select the casual loading checkbox if applicable. The calculator will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, and estimated tax and super. Remember, the results are estimates and do not include penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

For more information on award rates, casual loading, and average pay, explore our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion), [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading), and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) topics.

## Final Notes

Always verify your pay against the relevant award or enterprise agreement. The National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a target. Use the resources from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office to ensure compliance. Our calculator provides a quick estimate, but your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, and other factors.

### Additional Considerations for Part-Time Workers

If you work part-time, the same formula applies using your actual weekly hours. For example, 20 hours per week at $30/hour gives an annual gross of $30 × 20 × 52 = $31,200. Your fortnightly pay would be $1,200. The super guarantee still applies, and tax is calculated on the same brackets.

### Why Fortnightly Figures Help

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly gross and net pay can simplify budgeting. Our calculator provides both weekly and fortnightly estimates based on your hourly rate.

### The Role of Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. When using the calculator, tick the casual loading box to see the loaded rate. Do not manually add it to your entered rate.

### Superannuation on Top

Remember that super is paid on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. Your employer contributes an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base. This is separate from your take-home pay.

### Tax Brackets and Medicare in Practice

The tax brackets are progressive, meaning you only pay the higher rate on the portion of income above each threshold. The Medicare levy is a flat 2% on your taxable income, with possible reductions for low-income earners. Our calculator uses the single reduction thresholds from 2025–26 as a proxy.

### ADF Salary Sacrifice in Detail

ADF salary sacrifice can be structured through a salary packaging arrangement. Common benefits include additional super contributions, car leases, or electronic devices. By reducing your taxable income, you may move to a lower tax bracket and pay less Medicare levy. However, the super guarantee is still based on your ordinary time earnings before sacrifice. Our calculator does not model this, so use it as a starting point and seek professional advice.
